title: Grove takes accounting ownership of the Peg Stability Module while Sky keeps final control
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.6.1.1 has the PSM "directly managed and controlled by Sky" — setting debt ceilings, liquidity levels and asset management — until the Actively Stabilizing Collateral system is fully operational. A.2.8.2.2.2.6.1.2 then transfers a different thing: "Grove shall assume operational and accounting ownership of the PSM, incorporating the PSM's assets into its total value locked (TVL). Sky maintains active oversight and retains final control over strategic and operational decision-making within the PSM until full ASC implementation."

The two sentences allocate economics and authority to different parties. Grove books the assets, earns the yield and pays the Base Rate on them (A.2.8.2.2.2.6.2.1, A.2.8.2.2.2.6.2.2); Sky keeps the decision rights. Ownership here means exposure, not control.

The reason is that the PSM is systemically load-bearing. It is the mechanism holding USDS at its peg, so its debt ceilings and liquidity levels are stability parameters rather than a portfolio manager's choices. Handing those to a single Prime would delegate monetary policy; handing the economics avoids that while getting the asset actively managed by a party motivated to optimise it.

The TVL clause is not cosmetic. A.2.8.2.2.2.6.3.1 says PSM assets "count toward Grove's TVL, enhancing its economic standing and collateral efficiency," so Grove gains balance-sheet scale from assets whose strategic direction it does not set.

The arrangement is explicitly transitional in both directions — control returns to the question of ASC maturity, and A.2.8.2.2.2.6.3.2 anticipates Grove being able to "wind down the PSM entirely if ASC requirements are fulfilled through other mechanisms."
description: PSM assets count toward Grove's TVL and Grove pays the Base Rate on them, yet Sky keeps final say on strategic and operational decisions until the ASC system is fully implemented.
